slot.brief: Use the onto-function counting formula with inclusion–exclusion to count surjections between two small sets.

stem: Let $f$ and $g$ be functions from the real numbers to the real numbers, defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$ and $g(x)=x^2-4x+5$. How many real solutions does $f(g(x))=g(f(x))$ have?

verdicts.working: Equating the compositions gives [?;3;?m g(x)^2=(x^2-1)^2[?;0m, so either g(x)=x^2-1 or g(x)=-(x^2-1). The first yields x=3/2; the second has no real roots.

working:
$f(g(x))=g(x)^2+1$ and $g(f(x))=(x^2-1)^2+1$, so $g(x)^2=(x^2-1)^2$. Thus $g(x)=x^2-1$ or $g(x)=1-x^2$. The first gives $x=\dfrac{3}{2}$. The second gives $2x^2-4x+4=2((x-1)^2+1)=0$, which has no real solution. Hence there is exactly one real solution.

Independent check: Equating the compositions gives [?;3;?m g(x)^2=(x^2-1)^2[?;0m, so either g(x)=x^2-1 or g(x)=-(x^2-1). The first yields x=3/2; the second has no real roots.
solution:
Using $f(g(x))=g(x)^2+1$ and $g(f(x))=(x^2-1)^2+1$, equality requires
$$g(x)^2=(x^2-1)^2,$$
so $g(x)=x^2-1$ or $g(x)=1-x^2$. The first gives $x=\frac{3}{2}$; the second reduces to $(x-1)^2+1=0$, which has no real roots. Hence there is exactly $1$ real solution.
